title: Online survey of practice staff on influenza vaccination
summary:
Vaccinations save more than two million lives worldwide each year. Nevertheless, some individuals do not receive vaccinations or do not complete recommended vaccination schedules despite good accessibility, thereby showing vaccine hesitancy. A recommendation by healthcare professionals is a key determinant of vaccination decisions and may be influenced by the advisors’ own attitudes towards vaccination.

In Germany, most vaccinations are administered by general practitioners and pediatricians. Vaccinations recommended by the Ständige Impfkommission (STIKO) are fully reimbursed by statutory health insurance funds. Overall, vaccination coverage has declined both with increasing age and in recent years. Since general practitioners play a central role in vaccination, for their own protection and the protection of their patients, they occupy a key position in addressing existing gaps in vaccination coverage.

However, little is known about the vaccination attitudes of general practitioners in Germany. Therefore, this study investigates profession-specific influenza vaccination coverage rates in the outpatient German healthcare sector as well as potential reasons for the uptake or refusal of influenza vaccination.

To address the research questions, a one-time online survey will be conducted, aiming to achieve broad coverage of all practice staff in North Rhine-Westphalia.

interventions.name: A one-time online survey is planned among all staff members of general practices in North Rhine-Westphalia.
